title: Herpes zoster (shingles), adult
subject: infectious-disease
summary: Start oral valaciclovir, aciclovir or famciclovir within 72 hours of rash onset (later if new lesions, eye or ear involvement, or immunocompromise), refer ophthalmic zoster urgently, give IV aciclovir for disseminated, CNS or severe immunocompromised disease, and offer recombinant zoster vaccine.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Prodromal burning or tingling pain, then grouped vesicles on a red base in 1 or 2 adjacent dermatomes on one side; lesions crust in 7 to 10 days and heal in 2 to 4 weeks.
Herpes zoster ophthalmicus: vesicles on the forehead, eyelid, or tip or side of the nose (Hutchinson sign), red or painful eye, photophobia, reduced vision.
Ramsay Hunt syndrome: ear pain, vesicles in the ear canal or on the palate, facial palsy, hearing loss or vertigo.
Disseminated zoster: lesions in 3 or more dermatomes or widespread vesicles, or visceral disease (pneumonitis, hepatitis, encephalitis), mostly in immunocompromised patients.
Zoster in a young adult, or recurrent or multidermatomal zoster: offer an HIV test.

sections.title: Oral antivirals
items: Start within 72 hours of rash onset, especially if age over 50, moderate or severe pain or rash, or non-truncal (face, limb, genital) involvement.
Start even after 72 hours if new vesicles are still appearing, or with eye or ear involvement, complications or immunocompromise.

Valaciclovir 1 g orally three times daily for 7 days (fewer doses, better adherence), or aciclovir 800 mg orally five times daily for 7 days, or famciclovir 500 mg orally three times daily for 7 days.
Mild localised zoster in an immunocompromised patient can be treated orally with close follow-up; continue until all lesions have crusted.
Topical antivirals have no role. Keep lesions clean, dry and covered.

sections.title: IV aciclovir
items: Aciclovir 10 mg/kg IV every 8 hours (ideal body weight in obesity) for disseminated or visceral zoster, CNS involvement, severe ophthalmic disease, or severe immunocompromise (transplant, advanced HIV, chemotherapy).
Continue IV until no new lesions appear and the patient is improving, then switch to oral to complete at least 7 to 10 days; CNS disease needs 10 to 14 days of IV therapy.
Keep the patient well hydrated and monitor creatinine (crystal nephropathy) and mental state (neurotoxicity).
Renal adjustment of IV aciclovir: creatinine clearance 25 to 50 mL/min, 10 mg/kg every 12 hours; 10 to 25 mL/min, every 24 hours; below 10 mL/min, 5 mg/kg every 24 hours.

sections.title: Refer urgently
items: Ophthalmic zoster with eye symptoms, Hutchinson sign or reduced vision: same-day ophthalmology review, plus systemic antivirals.
Ramsay Hunt syndrome: ENT review.
Disseminated zoster, encephalitis, pneumonitis, or extensive disease in an immunocompromised patient: admit for IV aciclovir.

sections.title: Pain and special groups
items: Acute pain: paracetamol and NSAIDs, with a short opioid course if severe. Neuropathic pain or postherpetic neuralgia: amitriptyline 10 to 25 mg at night, or pregabalin 75 mg twice daily, or gabapentin 300 mg at night, titrated and adjusted for renal function.
Corticosteroids are not routinely recommended and do not prevent postherpetic neuralgia.

Renal impairment (valaciclovir): creatinine clearance 30 to 49 mL/min, 1 g every 12 hours; 10 to 29, 1 g every 24 hours; below 10, 500 mg every 24 hours. Elderly and CKD patients are prone to aciclovir neurotoxicity.
Pregnancy: aciclovir or valaciclovir can be used; involve obstetrics. A non-immune pregnant woman exposed to zoster needs specialist advice about varicella-zoster immunoglobulin.

sections.title: Infection control and vaccination
items: Localised zoster in an immunocompetent patient: cover lesions and use standard precautions; avoid contact with non-immune people and pregnant women until lesions crust.
Disseminated zoster, or any zoster in an immunocompromised patient: airborne and contact precautions until all lesions have crusted.

Recombinant zoster vaccine (Shingrix): 2 doses IM 2 to 6 months apart for adults 50 and older, and adults 19 and older who are or will be immunocompromised (second dose after 1 to 2 months if needed) (CDC).
Vaccinate whether or not there was prior zoster (not during the acute episode) and at least 8 weeks after live zoster vaccine; varicella serology screening is not needed.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Missing ophthalmic involvement: examine the eye and nose tip in every facial zoster.
Full-dose aciclovir or valaciclovir in CKD or the elderly without renal adjustment (confusion, AKI).
Withholding antivirals after 72 hours in a patient still forming new vesicles or with complications.
Nursing disseminated zoster without airborne precautions near non-immune staff or immunocompromised patients.

drugs.name: Valaciclovir
drugs.dose: 1 g orally three times daily for 7 days

drugs.name: Aciclovir (oral)
drugs.dose: 800 mg orally five times daily for 7 days

drugs.name: Famciclovir
drugs.dose: 500 mg orally three times daily for 7 days

drugs.name: Aciclovir (IV)
drugs.dose: 10 mg/kg IV every 8 hours (ideal body weight), 7 to 14 days depending on disease

drugs.name: Pregabalin
drugs.dose: 75 mg orally twice daily, titrated up to 300 mg twice daily
drugs.notes: Postherpetic neuralgia; reduce in renal impairment; sedation, dizziness.

drugs.name: Amitriptyline
drugs.dose: 10 to 25 mg orally at night, titrated to a maximum of 75 mg
drugs.notes: Avoid in cardiac conduction disease, glaucoma, urinary retention; caution in the elderly.

drugs.name: Recombinant zoster vaccine (Shingrix)
drugs.dose: 0.5 mL IM, 2 doses 2 to 6 months apart
drugs.notes: Age 50 and older, or 19 and older if immunocompromised.
